checks.title: Input contract validation
checks.instruction: Does a concrete path consume externally supplied input in a type, range or shape the visible contract does not permit, without a guard? Use only visible callers and contracts. A missing caller is insufficient evidence, not a proven bug.
checks.violation: An allowed external input reaches an incompatible operation without the required guard.
checks.no_violation: The relevant input is guarded before use, or the visible path has no externally supplied input.
checks.insufficient: The producer, caller or contract needed to prove the path is missing.

checks.title: Filesystem boundary
checks.instruction: Can an untrusted remote caller control a path or filename that reaches file access outside the caller's allowed boundary? Distinguish remote input from a local operator intentionally choosing a file. Do not assume a missing caller is remote.
checks.violation: A visible untrusted input bypasses the intended filesystem boundary and reaches outside it.
checks.no_violation: The path is confined to the allowed boundary or comes only from an authorized local operator/internal constant.
checks.insufficient: The input origin, authorization contract or boundary implementation is missing.

checks.title: Command injection
checks.instruction: Does visible untrusted data become executable shell syntax rather than a literal argument? Check the actual subprocess/shell API and data flow. Passing data in an argument array to a non-shell API is not shell injection by itself.
checks.violation: Untrusted input is interpolated into executable shell syntax on a reachable path.
checks.no_violation: Data is passed as literal arguments without shell interpretation, safely validated, or no shell execution occurs.
checks.insufficient: The command construction or execution API is not visible.

checks.title: Credential disclosure
checks.instruction: Does a concrete visible path disclose a credential value to logs, responses, persisted reports or an unintended recipient? Variable names, empty placeholders and intentional fictional test data alone do not prove a disclosure.
checks.violation: A credential value visibly reaches an unintended disclosure sink without redaction or access restriction.
checks.no_violation: The relevant value is redacted/confined, or no credential disclosure path is present.
checks.insufficient: The value origin or disclosure sink needed to establish exposure is not visible.

checks.title: Duplicate external side effects
checks.instruction: When an external side-effecting request may already have been accepted, can the visible retry path submit the same operation again without an idempotency guarantee or explicit authorization? Polling an existing operation is not a new submission.
checks.violation: An ambiguous accepted operation can be automatically submitted again without a visible deduplication contract.
checks.no_violation: The path reuses an existing operation, uses a documented idempotency guarantee, or has no such retry.
checks.insufficient: The side-effect or idempotency contract is not visible.

checks.title: Failure represented as success
checks.instruction: Does the visible error handling represent a failed operation as completed success, causing a caller to rely on missing or invalid output? A documented optional feature with an explicit unavailable result is not a hidden success.
checks.violation: A failure is hidden as successful output on a concrete visible path.
checks.no_violation: Failure remains observable or is handled by an explicit documented optional contract.
checks.insufficient: The return contract or consuming caller is needed to decide.

checks.title: Concurrent state integrity
checks.instruction: Does a concrete concurrent or interrupted path lose a state update or publish a partial result that a caller treats as complete? Look for actual read-modify-write and publication boundaries; do not infer a race only because a lock is outside the excerpt.
checks.violation: The supplied interleaving or interruption can concretely overwrite a valid update or publish an incomplete result.
checks.no_violation: The visible path serializes or atomically publishes the relevant update, or has no shared mutable state.
checks.insufficient: The locking, publication or caller contract is outside the supplied evidence.

checks.title: Concrete value-flow error
checks.instruction: For an input explicitly allowed by the visible contract, is there a concrete path that consumes a missing value or incompatible type and breaks execution? Do not flag style preferences, invented requirements or intentionally failing test fixtures.
checks.violation: An allowed input and visible value flow demonstrate a reproducible execution error.
checks.no_violation: The visible value uses agree with their contracts and guards.
checks.insufficient: Required input or producer contracts are missing.
